label: Bonus Class 3
title: Long and Short Vowels: Magic E and Vowel Teams
titleAr: الأصوات المتحركة الطويلة والقصيرة: E السحرية وفِرق الحروف المتحركة
bigIdea: Every English vowel letter has a short sound (cap) and a long sound that says its letter name (cape). A silent e at the end, or a vowel team like ai, ee, oa, is the spelling clue that tells us: say the long sound.
bigIdeaAr: لكل حرف متحرك في الإنجليزية صوت قصير (cap) وصوت طويل يُنطق كاسم الحرف (cape). وحرف e الصامت في آخر الكلمة، أو فريق الحروف المتحركة مثل ai و ee و oa، هو الدليل الإملائي الذي يقول لنا: انطق الصوت الطويل.
builtOn: Lessons 9-12: classroom commands, numbers to 100, months (May, June, July), My Birthday (cake, candle, present, balloon)
Phonics Lesson 9: R-blends (brush, crab, drum, frog, grass, tree)
Phonics Lesson 11: S-blends (spin, star, skip, smile, snail, swim)
Level 1 short vowels a, e, i, o, u; Bonus Class 1 (digraphs) and Bonus Class 2 (clusters)
Preview only (taught next): vowel teams ai, ee, oa in Lesson 13

objectives.en: I can hear the difference between a short vowel (cap) and a long vowel (cape).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أسمع الفرق بين الصوت القصير (cap) والصوت الطويل (cape).

objectives.en: I can use magic e to change a word: cap -> cape, kit -> kite, hop -> hope.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أستخدم E السحرية لأغيّر الكلمة: cap إلى cape و kit إلى kite و hop إلى hope.

objectives.en: I can read the vowel teams ai, ee and oa (rain, tree, boat).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أقرأ فِرق الحروف المتحركة ai و ee و oa (rain و tree و boat).

objectives.en: I can explain why the e in cake is silent (it used to be said, long ago).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أشرح لماذا لا تُنطق e في cake (كانت تُنطق قديماً).

keyTerms.meaning: The quick sound of a vowel: a in cap, i in kit, o in hop.
The vowel says its own letter name: a in cape, i in kite, o in hope.
An e at the end that we do not say. It jumps back over one consonant and makes the vowel say its name.
Two vowel letters that make one long sound: ai in rain, ee in tree, oa in boat.
A vowel that slides from one mouth shape to another: the a in cake slides e -> i.

linguisticsCorner.title: The mystery of the silent e

facts.en: About 600 years ago, the e at the end of words was spoken! 'Name' sounded like 'nah-muh' and 'kite' like 'kee-tuh'.
facts.ar: قبل نحو 600 سنة كان حرف e في آخر الكلمات يُنطق! كانت name تُنطق «نا-مَه» و kite تُنطق «كي-تَه».

facts.en: Then the final e went quiet, and over about 200 years the long vowels moved to new places in the mouth. Linguists call this the Great Vowel Shift.
facts.ar: ثم سكتت e الأخيرة، وعلى مدى نحو 200 سنة تحرّكت الأصوات الطويلة إلى أماكن جديدة في الفم. يسمّي علماء اللغة ذلك «التحوّل الكبير في الأصوات المتحركة».

facts.en: At the same time, printing arrived in England (1476) and spelling slowly stopped changing. So we still write the old spelling, but say the new sounds. The silent e is a fossil - and a useful clue: it tells us the vowel is long.
facts.ar: وفي الوقت نفسه وصلت الطباعة إلى إنجلترا (سنة 1476) وتوقّف الإملاء عن التغيّر شيئاً فشيئاً. لذلك ما زلنا نكتب التهجئة القديمة وننطق الأصوات الجديدة. e الصامتة أحفورة لغوية، لكنها دليل مفيد: تخبرنا أن الصوت طويل.

facts.en: English 'long' vowels are not just longer. Most of them slide: say cake slowly and your mouth moves from e to i. Linguists call these glides (diphthongs).
facts.ar: الأصوات «الطويلة» في الإنجليزية ليست أطول فقط، فمعظمها ينزلق: قل cake ببطء وستجد فمك ينتقل من e إلى i. يسمّيها علماء اللغة أصواتاً منزلقة.

facts.en: One sound, many spellings: the long a in cake, rain and May sounds the same but is spelled a-e, ai and ay. That is why English spelling needs detectives!
facts.ar: صوت واحد وتهجئات كثيرة: الصوت الطويل a في cake و rain و May واحد لكنه يُكتب a-e و ai و ay. لهذا تحتاج التهجئة الإنجليزية إلى محققين!

arabicBridge.english: short a / i / u in cap, kit, cub
arabicBridge.arabic: فتحة / كسرة / ضمة: بَ بِ بُ
arabicBridge.point: English short vowels are close to Arabic harakat. The difference: English always writes them as a full letter.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الأصوات القصيرة الإنجليزية قريبة من الحركات العربية، والفرق أن الإنجليزية تكتبها دائماً حرفاً كاملاً.

arabicBridge.english: long vowels in cape, kite, hope
arabicBridge.arabic: حروف المدّ: ا و ي (با، بو، بي)
arabicBridge.point: In Arabic a long vowel is the same vowel held longer (بَ -> با). In English the long vowel says the letter NAME and usually slides. So cape is not 'caap' (كاب); it is closer to 'kayp' (كيب).
arabicBridge.pointAr: في العربية الصوت الطويل هو الحركة نفسها ممدودة (بَ ثم با). أما في الإنجليزية فالصوت الطويل يُنطق كاسم الحرف وينزلق غالباً، فلا تُنطق cape «كاب» بل أقرب إلى «كيب».

arabicBridge.english: long i in kite, five, smile
arabicBridge.point: Standard Arabic بَيْت (bayt) has the same slide as English long i: a -> y. Arabic already has this sound!
arabicBridge.pointAr: في الفصحى كلمة «بَيْت» فيها الانزلاق نفسه الذي في long i الإنجليزية: من a إلى y. العربية تملك هذا الصوت!

arabicBridge.english: long a in cake, long o in home
arabicBridge.point: Egyptian and Gulf speech have pure long e and o (beet, yoom). English slides at the end: cake = ke-i-k, home = ho-u-m. Add a tiny smile (a) or a tiny round lip (o) at the end.
arabicBridge.pointAr: في اللهجات المصرية والخليجية صوتا e و o طويلان ثابتان (بيت، يوم). أما في الإنجليزية فينزلقان في النهاية: ابتسم ابتسامة صغيرة في آخر cake، واضمم شفتيك قليلاً في آخر home.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic also has letters that are written but not said, like the alif after waw al-jama'a in كتبوا. English silent e is similar: written, not said, but it has a job.
arabicBridge.pointAr: في العربية أيضاً حروف تُكتب ولا تُنطق، مثل الألف بعد واو الجماعة في «كتبوا». وكذلك e الصامتة في الإنجليزية: تُكتب ولا تُنطق، لكن لها وظيفة.

commonErrors.why: Reading every letter aloud, as Arabic reading usually does. The magic e is silent.
Not noticing the magic e, so the vowel stays short. Detective rule: look at the END of the word before you read the vowel.
Making the long vowel an Arabic alif (a longer fatha) instead of the letter name 'ay'.
Long o becomes Arabic waw (oo). English long o is the letter name O, with lips getting rounder at the end.

commonErrors.wrong: ship / sheep confused; fit / feet confused
commonErrors.why: Arabic kasra and ya differ mainly in length; English short i is also more relaxed and open than ee.

commonErrors.wrong: rayn read as ra-in; boat read as bo-at
commonErrors.why: Reading vowel teams letter by letter. Two vowels in a team make ONE long sound.

teacher: A 'magic e' wand (a pencil with a paper star) and an 'e' card
Word cards: cap/cape, tap/tape, mad/made, kit/kite, pin/pine, hop/hope, not/note, cub/cube, tub/tube
Vowel team cards: rain, snail, tree, green, sleep, boat, coat, road
Picture of an old printing press and a fossil
student: An 'e' card made in class (a big e on paper) to use as their magic e

stages.name: Warm-up: Snap or Stretch?
stages.method: TPR gestures (snap fingers for short, stretch arms for long) + Arabic hook
stages.purpose: Wake up the ear for vowel length using something the children already know in Arabic.
teacherSays: Detectives, in Arabic: كَتَبَ and كاتِب. Which one is longer? Yes, the alif makes ka into kaa.
Short sound: snap your fingers! Long sound: stretch your arms wide!
Listen: cap (snap!) ... cape (stre-e-etch!) ... kit (snap!) ... kite (stre-e-etch!)
Today's case: what makes English vowels long? Let's investigate!
teacherSaysAr: في العربية: كَتَبَ وكاتِب. أيهما أطول؟ الألف تمدّ الصوت.
الصوت القصير: طقطق بأصابعك. الصوت الطويل: افتح ذراعيك.
studentsDo: Snap or stretch for 8 quick words.
Say one Arabic pair with short and long vowels (e.g. دَرَسَ / دارِس).
tips: Pick clear pairs; the goal is to feel the contrast, not to explain it yet.
Gestures let you check all four children at once on camera.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: Harakat, Madd and Letter Names
stages.nameAr: جسر العربية: الحركات والمدّ وأسماء الحروف
stages.method: Contrastive analysis + mirror work + minimal-pair listening
stages.purpose: Link English short vowels to harakat, and show that English long vowels say their letter names and slide.
teacherSays: Short vowels are like harakat: cap is like fatha, kit like kasra, cub like damma.
Long vowels are different from Arabic madd. In Arabic, بَ becomes با: same sound, longer. In English, a long vowel says its NAME. Say the alphabet: A, E, I, O, U. That's the long sound!
Mirror: say A slowly... your mouth moves! e... i. It slides. Say I slowly: a... y. Like بَيْت in Fusha!
So cape is not caap. It is c-A-p. Say the letter name in the middle.
teacherSaysAr: الصوت القصير يشبه الحركة. أما الصوت الطويل في الإنجليزية فيُنطق كاسم الحرف: A و E و I و O و U.
انظر في المرآة: الفم يتحرك وينزلق، وليس مجرد مدّ للحركة كما في العربية.
studentsDo: Say the vowel letter names A, E, I, O, U slowly in the mirror and feel the slide.
Read بَيْت and kite and notice the same slide.
Listen to each word: snap (short) or stretch (long).

exercise.instructions: Listen. Short vowel (snap) or long vowel that says its name (stretch)?
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع: صوت قصير (طقطقة) أم صوت طويل يقول اسم الحرف (مدّ الذراعين)؟

tips: Be honest with the children: Arabic long vowels and English long vowels are cousins, not twins.
Long u (cube) says 'you'; there is a little y sound at the start. Children enjoy discovering this.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: The Silent E Fossil
stages.method: History storytelling with pictures (timeline) + true/false check
stages.purpose: Understand why English writes letters it does not say, and see magic e as a clue, not a trick.
teacherSays: Long, long ago - 600 years ago - English people SAID the e at the end. 'Name' was nah-muh. 'Kite' was kee-tuh!
Then the e went quiet. And slowly the long vowels moved in the mouth: kee became kite, nah became name. This is called the Great Vowel Shift.
But printing machines came to England in 1476, and spelling started to freeze. So we write the OLD spelling and say the NEW sounds.
The silent e is a fossil - like a dinosaur bone in a word! But it is a useful fossil: it tells you the vowel is long.
teacherSaysAr: قبل 600 سنة كانت e الأخيرة تُنطق! ثم سكتت وتحرّكت الأصوات الطويلة في الفم.
ثم جاءت الطباعة فتجمّد الإملاء. لذلك نكتب التهجئة القديمة وننطق الأصوات الجديدة. e الصامتة أحفورة مثل عظمة ديناصور!
studentsDo: Say the old pronunciations for fun: nah-muh, kee-tuh, mah-kuh.
Put three pictures in order on the slide: people say the e -> the e goes quiet -> printing freezes the spelling.
Answer the true/false quiz with thumbs.

exercise.instructions: True or false? Thumbs up or thumbs down.
exercise.instructionsAr: صح أم خطأ؟ إبهامك لأعلى أو لأسفل.

items.prompt: Long ago, the e at the end of 'name' was spoken.
We say the e at the end of 'cake' today.
Printing helped to freeze English spelling.
A silent e often tells us the vowel before it is long.
English long a is exactly the Arabic alif.
items.answer: false (it says the letter name and slides)

items.prompt: Arabic also has letters we write but do not say (like the alif in كتبوا).

tips: The fossil image is the key memory hook; ask children to draw a fossil 'e' in their notebook.
Keep dates light: '600 years ago' and 'printing' are enough for this age.

stages.name: Magic E Workshop: Wave the Wand
stages.method: Word transformation (phoneme substitution with a written cue) + gesture
stages.purpose: Read and spell CVC -> CVCe pairs and feel the rule: e jumps back over one consonant and makes the vowel say its name.
teacherSays: Here is cap. Short a. Now I wave my magic wand and add e at the end... The e is silent, but it jumps back over the p and taps the a. The a wakes up and says its NAME: cape!
Your turn: hold up your e card next to the word on the slide. What's the new word?
Detective rule: look at the END of the word first. Is there a magic e? Then the vowel says its name.
teacherSaysAr: e صامتة لكنها تقفز فوق حرف واحد وتلمس الحرف المتحرك فيقول اسمه.
قاعدة المحقق: انظر إلى آخر الكلمة أولاً.
studentsDo: Read the short word, hold their e card to the camera beside it, then read the long word.
Draw a jumping arrow from e back to the vowel.
Write each new word on paper.

exercise.instructions: Add magic e. Read the new word and write it.
exercise.instructionsAr: أضف E السحرية واقرأ الكلمة الجديدة واكتبها.

tips: Link to Lessons 11-12: cake (a-e) and June (u-e) are magic e words the children already know.
e-e words (Pete, these) are rare; mention them only to curious children.
Watch for children reading the e aloud: 'cak-eh'. Cover the e with a finger: 'It's a silent helper.'

stages.name: Vowel Teams Preview: When Two Vowels Go Walking
stages.nameAr: تمهيد لفِرق الحروف المتحركة: حين يمشي حرفان متحركان معاً
stages.method: Rule discovery with a chant + honest exceptions + word sort
stages.purpose: Meet ai, ee and oa before Lesson 13 and see that one long sound can have more than one spelling.
teacherSays: Another way to make a long vowel: a vowel team! Look: r-ai-n. Two vowels, one sound: A. The a says its name, the i is quiet.
The famous chant: 'When two vowels go walking, the first one does the talking!' rain, snail, boat, coat.
And ee? tree, green, sleep: the first e says its name E, the second is quiet.
Honest detective note: this chant works for ai, ee, oa - but NOT for every word in English. Detectives always check!
Now: cake and rain have the same sound, but different spellings. Sort the words by SOUND.
teacherSaysAr: حين يمشي حرفان متحركان معاً يتكلم الأول ويسكت الثاني.
تنبيه صادق: هذه القاعدة تنفع مع ai و ee و oa، لكنها لا تنطبق على كل الكلمات الإنجليزية.
studentsDo: Chant and walk two fingers across the desk for each vowel team.
Read rain, snail, tree, green, boat, coat aloud.
Sort words into three boxes by long sound: A, E or O.

exercise.instructions: Read the word. Which long sound: A, E or O? Underline the letters that make it.
exercise.instructionsAr: اقرأ الكلمة: أيّ صوت طويل فيها A أم E أم O؟ ضع خطاً تحت الحروف التي تصنعه.

tips: This is a preview: Lesson 13 teaches ai, ee, oa properly. Aim for recognition.
Have an exception ready for curious children: 'said' has ai but sounds like e. English spelling is old and full of surprises.

stages.name: Detective Sprint: Long or Short?
stages.method: Timed reading game with words from the R- and S-blend lessons (retrieval practice)
stages.purpose: Apply the long/short clues quickly in words that also have clusters, mixing Bonus 2 and Bonus 3 skills.
teacherSays: Speed round! A word flashes on the slide. Read it and shout 'short' or 'long'. Then tell me the clue: magic e, vowel team, or nothing.
Remember: no Sneaky Vowel in the cluster, and look at the end of the word!
Team points: one point for the right word, one point for the right clue.
teacherSaysAr: تظهر كلمة على الشاشة: اقرأها وقل short أو long، ثم أخبرني بالدليل: E السحرية أو فريق حروف متحركة أو لا شيء.
لا تنسَ: بلا حركة متسللة في التجمّع!
studentsDo: Read each word aloud in turn (one child per word, then the group checks).
Say short or long and the clue.
Keep a team score on paper.

exercise.instructions: Read the word. Short or long? What is the clue?
exercise.instructionsAr: اقرأ الكلمة: قصير أم طويل؟ وما الدليل؟

tips: Words come from the Lesson 9 and 11 phonics units, so the clusters are familiar.
If a child says 'sil-ide', send in the red ghost from Bonus Class 2: two skills in one word.

stages.name: Production: Magic E Birthday Card
stages.nameAr: إنتاج: بطاقة عيد ميلاد بـE السحرية
stages.method: Creative writing with a word bank + read-aloud and peer check
stages.purpose: Use long-vowel words in real sentences connected to the Lesson 12 birthday topic.
teacherSays: Let's write a birthday card! Use at least three long-vowel words: cake, smile, made, nine, five, June, July, home, kite, game.
Example: 'Happy birthday! I made a cake. You are nine. Smile!'
Read your card to the group. Listeners: catch every magic e word and say if it was long.
teacherSaysAr: اكتب بطاقة عيد ميلاد فيها ثلاث كلمات على الأقل بصوت طويل.
المستمعون: التقطوا كل كلمة فيها E السحرية.
studentsDo: Write a 3-4 sentence birthday card and underline the long-vowel words.
Read it aloud to the camera.
Listeners give one star for each correct long vowel.
tips: nine and five show magic e in numbers; June shows long u; July has long i spelled y (a bonus discovery).
Accept simple sentences; the target is the vowel, not the grammar.

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Goodbye
stages.method: Formative check (read and write) + curiosity close
stages.purpose: Check magic e reading and spelling, and send home the fossil fact.
teacherSays: Exit ticket: read the five words and write S for short or L for long.
Did you know? 600 years ago, 'kite' sounded like 'kee-tuh'. The silent e is a fossil from that time!
Mission: find 5 magic e words at home and show your family the magic wand trick.
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ قبل 600 سنة كانت kite تُنطق «كي-تَه». e الصامتة أحفورة من ذلك الزمن!
مهمتك: جد 5 كلمات فيها E السحرية وأرِ عائلتك خدعة العصا السحرية.
studentsDo: Read 5 words and write S or L.
Say goodbye with a long vowel: 'Bye! See you!'
tips: Note children who still read the e aloud; give them cap/cape card pairs in Lesson 13 warm-ups.

exitTicket.instructions: Read the word. Write S (short vowel) or L (long vowel).
exitTicket.instructionsAr: اقرأ الكلمة واكتب S للصوت القصير أو L للصوت الطويل.

homework.en: Magic E Hunt: find 5 words with magic e at home (on boxes, books or in your Lesson 12 words) and write them. Then make 4 magic e pairs yourself (cap/cape...) and read them to a family member. Tell them the fossil story.
homework.ar: البحث عن E السحرية: جد 5 كلمات فيها E السحرية في البيت (على العلب أو في الكتب أو في كلمات الدرس 12) واكتبها. ثم اصنع 4 أزواج بنفسك (cap/cape...) واقرأها لأحد أفراد أسرتك، واحكِ له قصة الأحفورة.
tasks: Write 5 magic e words and draw the jumping arrow from e to the vowel.
Make 4 short/long pairs and read them aloud.
Write one word each with ai, ee and oa and draw a picture.

support: Use only a and i (cap/cape, kit/kite) before adding o and u.
Give each word as a pair on one card so the child compares directly.
Let the child physically cover and uncover the e with a finger while reading.
challenge: Find words where magic e does NOT make a long vowel: have, give, love, come. Why? (Old spellings again!)
Find three spellings of long a: cake, rain, May (a-e, ai, ay).
Make your own magic e pairs (fin/fine, cut/cute, rid/ride) and teach them to the group.

successCriteria: Hears short vs long in at least 6 of 8 listening items.
Reads and writes at least 8 of 10 magic e transformations correctly.
Reads rain, tree and boat with one long vowel sound each.
Explains in English or Arabic why the e is silent or what it does.
watchFor: long a said as Arabic alif (caap)
vowel teams read as two sounds (ra-in)

teacherNotes: 'Long vowels say their letter name' is a classic phonics simplification. Phonetically, long a /eɪ/, long i /aɪ/ and long o /əʊ/ or /oʊ/ are diphthongs, and long u is /juː/. Use 'says its name' with the children and 'slides' when they mishear.
Be honest that Arabic long vowels (madd) are not the same: they are longer harakat. English long vowels change quality.
Vowel teams ai, ee, oa are taught in Lesson 13; this class prepares the idea and the chant.
Common exceptions (have, give, come, said) are real; present them as 'old spellings' so the rule stays useful without being false.
Bonus Class 4 finishes the level with syllables, stress and the three sounds of -s.
